prize_parts.citation: For the design of ionizable lipids and their assembly into lipid nanoparticles that enable systemic delivery of nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B040, a single prize part. The round-1 exchange sharpened rather than weakened the case. No member called it unworthy, and the objections concern attribution and recency, not science. The chemistry is a simple structure-property rule: a lipid whose apparent pKa keeps the particle near-neutral in blood and charged in the acidifying endosome, assembled by rapid mixing into particles that carry a polyanion across a membrane. It is independently validated at scale (patisiran, then the COVID-19 vaccines). I would write the citation around the lipid chemistry (ionizable lipid design and assembly) and not around vaccines or formulation, which answers the chair's question and keeps it complementary to the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside modification, which honoured the cargo and not the vehicle. On the chair's B040 versus B004 question I prefer the newer modality with a contested trio over the mature method with a clean pair, because the 2010 overlap weighs on B004 and the contested trio is a problem of choosing among deserving people, not a problem of whether the discovery is real.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point and I cannot settle it from the files. My trio rests on a reading of the record that Cullis anchored the Vancouver work, that MacLachlan and Cullis carried the ionizable-lipid optimisation that made systemic siRNA work in vivo, and that Anderson's lipidoid libraries opened a second, potent route to ionizable lipids. A Cullis, Madden and Hope trio, as Chabes proposed, is a defensible alternative that values the earliest formulation work, and Langer is excluded by every trio. I also accept that some will read this as formulation engineering, and as a second prize for the mRNA story after 2023. If the expert report shows that the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid principle was first demonstrated by a different subset than mine, my second and third names should change, though Cullis should not.

responses.point: Chabes holds that the core lipid-nanoparticle concept belongs to the Vancouver group of Cullis, Madden and Hope, and that a prize requiring arbitration between that lineage and the lipidoid lineage looks fragile.
responses.response: I agree that the choice between the two lineages is a judgment about which step is decisive, and I do not claim it is a clean fact. My answer is that the citation should reward what determines the modern product: the ionizable lipid whose pKa is tuned for endosomal release, not the earlier liposome formulation and remote loading. That is why I keep MacLachlan and Anderson beside Cullis and leave Hope and Madden out, a cut I regret. I would test both trios against the primary literature as Daniel Aili suggests, but fragility of attribution is a reason for a careful citation and not for abandoning a discovery with this much evidence behind it.

responses.point: Somfai ranks B004 first, argues that C-N coupling needed a different ligand and mechanistic solution from the 2010 C-C work, and calls the Buchwald and Hartwig attribution unusually clean.
responses.response: Your separation of the C-N problem (amine binding, deprotonation, difficult reductive elimination, suppressing beta-hydride elimination) from the C-C precedent is convincing and I have dropped any suggestion that B004 is a mere repeat. It remains my first alternative, and I would not oppose it if the committee prefers a clean pair. What keeps B040 first for me is that the prize would recognise a new class of medicine that did not exist as a modality, while B004 completes a field recognised in 2010. I also accept your warning that a clean attribution is worth a great deal, so I treat the contested trio as the cost I am knowingly accepting.

responses.point: Zou prefers B004 and says Anderson's lipidoid work is a different contribution from the pKa-tuned lipid and rapid-mixing formulation principle, so the committee should decide whether the citation is the formulation principle before accepting a trio.
responses.response: This is a fair challenge and I have tried to meet it in the citation. It now names ionizable lipid design and assembly, which is the Cullis and MacLachlan line, and Anderson enters because the lipidoid libraries showed that the same ionizable-lipid principle yields potent in vivo delivery by a second, independent route that fed into the later mRNA products. If the committee thinks that is a different contribution, the honest alternative is a Vancouver-only trio and not a Cullis-Anderson hybrid with the logic hidden. I would rather make the choice openly in the citation than leave it implicit.

responses.point: Linke prefers Car-Parrinello (B021) for its single idea and two-author attribution, and the chair asked whether I would move my first choice given that B021 has no other first-place support.
responses.response: I keep B021 as my second alternative, with real respect for the idea and the clean credit. Two things hold me back. Its consequences run largely through specialist successors and descendants, whereas B040 can be traced to products that changed what clinicians can do, which is the game-changer test I apply. And with computational prizes in 2013 and 2024, a third in roughly a decade is a recency cost I would weigh seriously. I also have to be careful as someone from the same simulation tradition, so I decline to be the advocate for B021; I would hand that role to you.

responses.point: Sparr prefers B040 with Cullis, Anderson and MacLachlan, anchors the case in lipid phase behaviour and rapid-mixing assembly, and warns that her closeness to lipid self-assembly could lead her to overweight it.
responses.response: We reached the same trio independently, which is some reassurance but not evidence, since neither of us has verified priority. Your lipid-phase framing is what makes this a chemistry prize, and I have borrowed it by naming ionizable lipid design and assembly in the citation. I would still ask you, as the chair requested, to say which assembly steps are decisive for endosomal escape: the pKa window, the shift to a non-bilayer phase, or the PEG-lipid control of particle size. The answer determines whether MacLachlan's optimisation or Anderson's library screening deserves the third place.

uncertainties: Which of Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer first demonstrated the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid principle for in vivo nucleic-acid delivery; my trio rests on recollection and should be checked against the primary literature and the expert report.
Whether the committee will accept a delivery chemistry prize shortly after the 2023 Medicine mRNA prize as complementary, and whether it will treat it as chemistry and not pharmaceutical engineering.
Whether the committee prefers a newer modality with a contested trio (B040) or a mature method with a clean pair (B004).
Whether the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes make a simulation prize (B021) unlikely, which bears on my second alternative.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional tie to any candidate in B040, B004 or B021, and no recusal sought. My Warshel-school background and familiarity with the biomolecular simulation community around Parrinello (B021) is scientific familiarity only, so I step back from advocating B021 and keep it only as an alternative. Unchanged from round 1.
